metadata.document_title: Responsible use of artificial intelligence in surveying practice

definitions.text: Set requirements or expectations for RICS members and regulated firms about how they provide services or the outcomes of their actions. Principles-based and focused on outcomes and good practice. Mandatory requirements use the word 'must' and must be complied with. Recommended best practice uses the word 'should' — acceptable alternatives may achieve the same or better outcome.

Information to support practice, knowledge and performance of RICS members and regulated firms. Includes definitions, processes, toolkits, checklists, insights, research and technical information. Not mandatory and does not set requirements or make explicit recommendations.

A machine-based system that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments. Different AI systems vary in their levels of autonomy and adaptiveness after deployment. There are many types (narrow and general AI) and subsets (machine learning and natural language processing). AI systems may be embedded within a broader technological solution.
definitions.source: OECD Explanatory Memorandum on the Updated OECD Definition of an AI System, March 2024

definitions.text: A particular way in which an AI system might fail to perform its function.

Information that must not be unlawfully obtained, used or disclosed. Includes personal data (any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person — see UK GDPR) and may include commercially sensitive data.
An attitude that includes a questioning mind, critically assessing evidence relied on and being alert to conditions that may cause information provided to be misleading.
definitions.source: RICS Valuation — Global Standards, PS 2, section 1, paragraph 1.5

definitions.text: The level of risk that an organisation or individual is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives. Five categories: averse, minimalist, cautious, open, ambitious.

A register documenting all identified risks facing an organisation. Typically records: description of each risk, likelihood and impact, mitigation plans, risk appetite of the firm, and regular updates to status and progress.

context_entries.title: Material Impact Threshold
context_entries.text: This standard applies to the outputs of AI systems that have a material impact on the delivery of the surveying service. Whether an output has a material impact depends on whether it is capable of influencing the delivery of the service and the nature of the influence it exerts, based on the facts and circumstances of output use. Examples include: outputs summarising documents relied on in reports, outputs composing significant parts of an opinion, or outputs recommending which part of a building to investigate for a fault.

context_entries.title: Global Applicability and Legislative Override
context_entries.text: This standard sets requirements for members and RICS-regulated firms in all jurisdictions globally. If this standard conflicts with legislation in any jurisdiction, the legislation takes precedence.

rules.requirement_text: If a member or regulated firm determines that their use of AI systems will have a material impact on the delivery of surveying services, they must make a record of that determination and the reasoning behind it.
rules.trigger: Determination that AI use has material impact on service delivery.
rules.evidence_implied: Written record of materiality determination with supporting reasoning.
rules.source_text_verbatim: If an RICS member or regulated firm determines that their use of AI systems will have a material impact on the delivery of surveying services, then they must make a record of that determination and the reasoning behind it.

rules.requirement_text: Members and RICS-regulated firms must comply with RICS professional standards and with any relevant legislation that applies in the relevant jurisdiction (such as EU Regulation 2024/1689).
rules.trigger: Use of AI systems in any jurisdiction where RICS standards apply.
rules.evidence_implied: Documented compliance with applicable RICS standards and local legislation; policy or compliance register.
rules.source_text_verbatim: Members and RICS-regulated firms must comply with RICS professional standards and with any relevant legislation that applies in the relevant jurisdiction (such as EU Regulation 2024/1689).

rules.requirement_text: If this standard conflicts with legislation in any jurisdiction, the legislation takes precedence, but members and RICS-regulated firms must make a record of the conflict and report it to RICS.
rules.trigger: Identified conflict between this RICS standard and local legislation.
rules.evidence_implied: Written record of the legislative conflict; evidence of report to RICS.
rules.source_text_verbatim: If this standard conflicts with legislation in any jurisdiction, the legislation takes precedence, but members and RICS-regulated firms must make a record of the conflict and report it to RICS.

rules.section_title: Baseline knowledge for using AI in surveying
rules.parent_section_title: Baseline knowledge for using AI in surveying
rules.requirement_text: Members who use AI systems to deliver surveying services must develop and maintain sufficient and appropriate knowledge to support their responsible use of those systems.
rules.trigger: Use of AI systems in the delivery of surveying services.
rules.evidence_implied: Training records, CPD logs, certificates, learning activity records.
rules.source_text_verbatim: Members who use AI systems to deliver surveying services must develop and maintain sufficient and appropriate knowledge to support their responsible use of those systems.

rules.section_title: Baseline knowledge for using AI in surveying
rules.parent_section_title: Baseline knowledge for using AI in surveying
rules.requirement_text: Members who use AI systems must ensure they have a basic understanding of the different types and subsets of AI system and their basic ways of working, limitations and failure modes.
rules.trigger: Use of AI systems in surveying services.
rules.evidence_implied: Demonstrable understanding of AI system types, how they work, limitations, and failure modes.
rules.source_text_verbatim: the different types and subsets of AI system and their basic ways of working, limitations and failure modes

rules.section_title: Baseline knowledge for using AI in surveying
rules.parent_section_title: Baseline knowledge for using AI in surveying
rules.requirement_text: Members who use AI systems must have a basic understanding of the risk of AI systems producing erroneous output.
rules.trigger: Use of AI systems in surveying services.
rules.evidence_implied: Demonstrable awareness of error risks in AI outputs.
rules.source_text_verbatim: the risk of AI systems producing erroneous output

rules.section_title: Baseline knowledge for using AI in surveying
rules.parent_section_title: Baseline knowledge for using AI in surveying
rules.requirement_text: Members who use AI systems must have a basic understanding of the inherent risk of bias in AI systems.
rules.trigger: Use of AI systems in surveying services.
rules.evidence_implied: Demonstrable awareness of bias risks in AI systems.
rules.source_text_verbatim: the inherent risk of bias in AI systems

rules.section_title: Baseline knowledge for using AI in surveying
rules.parent_section_title: Baseline knowledge for using AI in surveying
rules.requirement_text: Members who use AI systems must have a basic understanding of data usage and data risks relevant to the use of AI systems.
rules.trigger: Use of AI systems in surveying services.
rules.evidence_implied: Demonstrable understanding of AI-related data usage and associated risks.
rules.source_text_verbatim: data usage and data risks relevant to the use of AI systems

rules.requirement_text: RICS-regulated firms that use AI systems must safeguard any private and confidential data they hold.
rules.trigger: Use of AI systems where private and confidential data is held.
rules.evidence_implied: Data governance policy; data security protocols; evidence of sub-requirements RICS-S3.1-02 through RICS-S3.1-06.
rules.source_text_verbatim: RICS-regulated firms that use AI systems must safeguard any private and confidential data they hold, including by:

rules.requirement_text: Private and confidential data must be stored securely, for example by using encryption and/or backing up the data stored.
rules.trigger: Storage of private and confidential data by the firm.
rules.evidence_implied: Encryption policies; backup procedures; IT security documentation.
rules.source_text_verbatim: storing private and confidential data securely, for example by using encryption and/or backing up the data stored

rules.requirement_text: Access to private and confidential data held by the firm must be restricted to staff who strictly need access.
rules.trigger: Use or storage of private and confidential data in connection with AI systems.
rules.evidence_implied: Access control lists; role-based access policies; access logs.
rules.source_text_verbatim: restricting access to private and confidential data held by the firm to staff that strictly need access

rules.requirement_text: Staff with access to private and confidential data must receive regular training, at least annually, so that they are aware of and equipped to manage the risks to privacy and confidentiality posed by the use of AI.
rules.trigger: Staff having access to private and confidential data used with AI systems.
rules.evidence_implied: Annual training records; training content/materials; attendance logs; competence assessments.
rules.source_text_verbatim: regularly (at least annually) training staff with such access so that they are aware of and are equipped to manage the risks to privacy and confidentiality posed by the use of AI

rules.requirement_text: Data must be prepared for use in AI systems in a way that protects privacy, such as by anonymising it.
rules.trigger: Preparation of data for input into AI systems.
rules.evidence_implied: Data preparation procedures; anonymisation records; data handling logs.
rules.source_text_verbatim: preparing data for use in a way that protects privacy, such as by anonymising it

rules.requirement_text: Firms must refrain from uploading private and confidential data to AI systems, except where BOTH: (a) there is express written consent in advance from affected stakeholders, AND (b) the firm has taken reasonable steps to satisfy itself that uploading the data does not pose an unacceptable risk.
rules.trigger: Any proposed upload of private or confidential data to an AI system.
rules.evidence_implied: Written consent records from stakeholders; risk assessment for data uploads; upload logs with justification.
rules.source_text_verbatim: refraining from uploading private and confidential data to AI systems, except where: there is express written consent in advance from affected stakeholders to do so and the firm has taken reasonable steps to satisfy itself that uploading data to the AI system in question does not pose an unacceptable risk.

rules.requirement_text: Before using an AI system that will have a material impact on service delivery, firms must carry out and record in writing an assessment of whether AI is the most appropriate tool to use.
rules.trigger: Intended use of an AI system with material impact on surveying services.
rules.evidence_implied: Written assessment document or policy statement evaluating AI appropriateness.
rules.source_text_verbatim: Before using an AI system that will have a material impact on service delivery, RICS-regulated firms must have carried out — and recorded in writing — an assessment of whether AI is the most appropriate tool to use

rules.requirement_text: The assessment of whether AI is the most appropriate tool must consider at least: (a) the surveying services provided by the firm, (b) the nature of the task or process, (c) available alternative tools, (d) environmental impact information, (e) stakeholder impact information, (f) data risks, and (g) the risk of erroneous output and bias and their consequences.
rules.trigger: Conducting the appropriateness assessment per RICS-S3.2-01.
rules.evidence_implied: Written assessment addressing all seven considerations; comparison documentation.
rules.source_text_verbatim: having considered at least: the surveying services provided by the firm; the nature of the task or process for which AI could be used; available alternative tools for executing the task or process; environmental impact information available for all tools being considered; stakeholder impact information available for all tools being considered; data risks and from the information available, the risk of erroneous output from, and the risk of bias inherent in, the AI system(s) being considered, and the consequences should these risks materialise.

rules.requirement_text: Firms must maintain a written register of AI systems that have a material impact on service delivery, including: (a) the AI system used, (b) the purpose for which it is used, (c) the date of first use, and (d) the next review date.
rules.trigger: Use of AI systems with material impact on surveying services.
rules.evidence_implied: Written AI systems register with all four fields populated and current.
rules.source_text_verbatim: RICS-regulated firms must also maintain a written register that includes details of: any AI system used that has a material impact on the delivery of surveying services; the purpose for which that AI system is used; the date on which that AI system was first used and the date on which the use and appropriateness of that AI system for the particular task or process will next be reviewed.

rules.requirement_text: Firms that use or intend to use AI systems must develop and implement policies regarding the responsible use of AI systems, informed by a risk register. These policies must cover both internally developed AI systems and those provided by third parties.
rules.trigger: Use or intended use of AI systems in surveying services.
rules.evidence_implied: Written responsible AI use policy informed by risk register; coverage of internal and third-party AI.
rules.source_text_verbatim: RICS-regulated firms that use or intend to use AI systems in the delivery of surveying services must develop and implement policies regarding the responsible use of AI systems, informed by a risk register (section 3.3).

rules.requirement_text: Responsible use policies must detail and clarify the roles, responsibilities and liabilities of all individuals involved in the procurement and/or use of AI.
rules.trigger: Development of responsible AI use policy.
rules.evidence_implied: Policy section or RACI matrix detailing roles, responsibilities, liabilities.
rules.source_text_verbatim: detail and clarify the roles, responsibilities and liabilities of all individuals involved in the procurement and/or use of AI

rules.requirement_text: Responsible use policies must detail the regular (at least annual), relevant training expectations for all individuals involved in the procurement and/or use of AI.
rules.trigger: Development of responsible AI use policy.
rules.evidence_implied: Training plan/schedule in policy; training records; competence matrix.
rules.source_text_verbatim: detail the regular (at least annual), relevant training expectations for all individuals involved in the procurement and/or use of AI

rules.requirement_text: Responsible use policies must state how human control and judgement is to interact with the use of AI systems, such as through regular monitoring or dip-samples of outputs for quality assurance purposes.
rules.trigger: Development of responsible AI use policy.
rules.evidence_implied: Policy section describing human oversight mechanisms; monitoring procedures; QA dip-sampling protocols.
rules.source_text_verbatim: state how human control and judgement is to interact with the use of AI systems, such as through regular monitoring or dip-samples of outputs for quality assurance purposes

rules.requirement_text: Responsible use policies must provide guidance to staff on how to identify and mitigate risks involved in the use of AI systems.
rules.trigger: Development of responsible AI use policy.
rules.evidence_implied: Risk identification guidance in policy; risk mitigation procedures; staff guidance documentation.
rules.source_text_verbatim: provide guidance to staff on how to identify and mitigate risks involved in the use of AI systems

rules.requirement_text: Firms using AI systems with material impact on service delivery must create and operate a risk register documenting risks associated with AI use.
rules.trigger: Use of AI systems with material impact on surveying services.
rules.evidence_implied: Active, maintained risk register document.
rules.source_text_verbatim: RICS-regulated firms using AI systems that have a material impact on the delivery of surveying services must create and operate a risk register:

rules.requirement_text: The risk register must document overarching risks including: (a) inherent bias in the AI system and its outputs, (b) erroneous outputs, (c) limitations to information available about the AI system and training data, and (d) retention and/or use of data inputted by the firm.
rules.trigger: Creation and maintenance of the risk register.
rules.evidence_implied: Risk register entries covering all four overarching risk categories.
rules.source_text_verbatim: that documents overarching risks associated with the use of AI, including: inherent bias in the AI system and its outputs; erroneous outputs from the AI system; limitations to the quantity and quality of information available regarding the AI system and its underlying training data, and retention and/or use of data inputted by the firm into the AI system.

rules.requirement_text: For each risk in the register, the following must be included: (a) description, (b) likelihood and impact, (c) mitigation plan, (d) firm's risk appetite, (e) regular status updates, and (f) RAG rating or similar categorisation.
rules.trigger: Documenting individual risks in the risk register.
rules.evidence_implied: Risk register with all six fields populated for each risk entry.
rules.source_text_verbatim: that for each risk includes: a description of the risk; the likelihood of the risk materialising and its likely impact; the plan to mitigate and manage the risk; the risk appetite of the firm; regular updates to the status and progress of risk management, and a categorisation of the risk according to a red, amber, green (RAG) rating, or similar method.

rules.requirement_text: The risk register must be reviewed and updated at least quarterly by staff who are responsible for making decisions about the firm's use of AI.
rules.trigger: Ongoing operation of the risk register.
rules.evidence_implied: Quarterly review records; timestamps/version history; sign-off by responsible decision-makers.
rules.source_text_verbatim: The risk register must be reviewed and updated at least quarterly by staff at RICS-regulated firms who are responsible for making decisions about the firm's use of AI.

rules.requirement_text: Firms must carry out detailed due diligence before procuring from a third-party supplier an AI system that will have a material impact on the delivery of surveying services.
rules.trigger: Procurement of a third-party AI system with material impact on services.
rules.evidence_implied: Completed due diligence file/checklist for each procured AI system.
rules.source_text_verbatim: RICS-regulated firms must therefore carry out detailed due diligence before procuring from a third-party supplier an AI system (whether embedded in a broader technological solution or not) that will have a material impact on the delivery of surveying services.

rules.requirement_text: The detailed due diligence must involve: (a) requesting information in writing from the supplier, (b) following up in writing as necessary, (c) recording and assessing information to inform procurement decisions and risk documentation, and (d) keeping a record of practical testing for fitness for purpose.
rules.trigger: Conducting due diligence on a third-party AI system.
rules.evidence_implied: Written correspondence with supplier; information assessment records; testing records/logs.
rules.source_text_verbatim: This detailed due diligence must involve: requesting information in writing from the third-party supplier; following up such requests in writing as necessary; recording the information provided, and assessing it to inform decisions about procurement, use and associated risks (including risks to be documented in the risk register) regarding the AI system, and keeping a record of the extent to which practical testing of an AI system for fitness for purpose has been carried out.

rules.requirement_text: If a supplier provides no or only limited information, firms must identify the risks associated with any missing information and record them in the risk register.
rules.trigger: Supplier provides insufficient information during due diligence.
rules.evidence_implied: Risk register entries for information gaps; documented risk assessment of missing information.
rules.source_text_verbatim: If a supplier provides no or only limited information, RICS-regulated firms must identify the risks associated with any missing information and record them in the risk register.

rules.requirement_text: The detailed due diligence must involve written requests for at minimum: (a) environmental impact of the AI system, (b) stakeholders involved in development, (c) compliance with data and confidentiality laws, (d) permissions obtained for individual data use, (e) accuracy, relevance and diversity of training datasets including known gaps and bias risks, and (f) type and extent of third-party provider liability.
rules.trigger: Conducting due diligence on a third-party AI system.
rules.evidence_implied: Written requests to supplier covering all six topics; supplier responses or documented non-responses.
rules.source_text_verbatim: The detailed due diligence must involve written requests for the following information, as a minimum: the environmental impact of the AI system; stakeholders involved in the development of the AI system; compliance with applicable data and confidentiality laws; permissions obtained where data and content relating to individuals have been used; the accuracy, relevance and diversity of the datasets used to train the AI, including any known gaps in the data, noting any particular known risks of bias, and the type and extent of the liability of the third-party provider.

rules.requirement_text: Members and firms must apply their professional judgement (knowledge, skills, experience and professional scepticism) to make a decision about the reliability of the output of any AI system used with material impact on service delivery.
rules.trigger: Use of AI system output with material impact on service delivery.
rules.evidence_implied: Decision log or assessment record demonstrating application of professional judgement.
rules.source_text_verbatim: RICS members and regulated firms using AI systems must therefore apply their professional judgement to make a decision about the reliability of the output of any AI system used that will have a material impact on the delivery of surveying services. Professional judgement consists of: knowledge; skills; experience and professional scepticism.

rules.requirement_text: Members and firms must document their decision about the reliability of the output in writing.
rules.trigger: Decision made about AI output reliability per RICS-S4.2-01.
rules.evidence_implied: Written reliability decision document.
rules.source_text_verbatim: RICS members and regulated firms must document their decision about the reliability of the output in writing.

rules.requirement_text: A written reliability decision must detail: (a) relevant assumptions made, (b) key areas of concern regarding reliability including underlying datasets, (c) the reason for each concern, (d) whether anything could lessen each concern, and (e) the impact on overall reliability including a conclusion on fitness for intended purpose.
rules.trigger: Preparation of written reliability decision per RICS-S4.2-02.
rules.evidence_implied: Written reliability decision addressing all five items; documented assumptions; concern analysis with mitigations; fitness-for-purpose conclusion.
rules.source_text_verbatim: A written decision about the reliability of any given output by a member or RICS-regulated firm must detail: any relevant assumptions made; key areas of concern regarding reliability, including the reliability of any underlying datasets; the reason for each concern; whether anything could be done to lessen each concern and the impact of the concern(s) on the overall reliability of the output, including a statement concluding whether the member or RICS-regulated firm considers that the output can reasonably be used for its intended purpose.

rules.requirement_text: A written reliability decision must be prepared by, or under the supervision of, an appropriately qualified and named surveyor who accepts responsibility for its use.
rules.trigger: Preparation of written reliability decision.
rules.evidence_implied: Named surveyor sign-off on reliability decision; documentation of qualifications and supervisory role.
rules.source_text_verbatim: A written decision about the reliability of any given output by a member or RICS-regulated firm must be prepared by, or under the supervision of, an appropriately qualified and named surveyor who accepts responsibility for its use.

rules.requirement_text: Where members or firms determine that an output cannot reasonably be used for its intended purpose, they must communicate that conclusion in writing to clients, together with their reasoning or a summary of it.
rules.trigger: Determination that an AI output is unreliable for its intended purpose.
rules.evidence_implied: Written client communication of unreliability conclusion with reasoning.
rules.source_text_verbatim: Where members or RICS-regulated firms determine that an output cannot reasonably be used for its intended purpose, they must communicate such a conclusion in writing to clients, together with their written reasoning or a summary of it.

rules.requirement_text: Where AI is used to automate outputs or produce high volumes of outputs, members and firms must undertake randomised dip samples at regular intervals to scrutinise and assure quality.
rules.trigger: Use of AI for automated or high-volume output generation.
rules.evidence_implied: Dip-sampling protocol; sampling logs with dates and results; quality assurance records.
rules.source_text_verbatim: RICS members and regulated firms must therefore undertake randomised dip samples of the outputs at regular intervals, so that they can scrutinise and assure the quality of outputs.

rules.section_title: Terms of engagement and client communication
rules.requirement_text: Members and firms that use AI systems with a material impact on service delivery must make clear to clients, in writing and in advance of using those AI systems, when and for what purpose AI is to be used.
rules.trigger: Use of AI systems with material impact, prior to commencement.
rules.evidence_implied: Written advance disclosure to client; signed engagement letter or equivalent.
rules.source_text_verbatim: Members and RICS-regulated firms that use AI systems with a material impact on the delivery of surveying services must therefore make clear to clients, in writing and in advance of using those AI systems, when and for what purpose AI is to be used.

rules.section_title: Terms of engagement and client communication
rules.requirement_text: Terms of engagement and related documentation must detail in writing: (a) when AI will be involved, (b) which parts of the service process use AI, (c) extent of PI cover for AI use if available, (d) internal processes to contest AI use, (e) processes to seek redress if negatively affected, and (f) how client can opt out of AI use if at all.
rules.trigger: Establishing terms of engagement with client where AI is to be used.
rules.evidence_implied: Updated terms of engagement addressing all six items; client sign-off.
rules.source_text_verbatim: The terms of engagement, contractual documents, service agreements and other relevant documentation used by members and RICS-regulated firms to govern their client relationships must detail in writing: when AI will be involved in the delivery of a surveying service; the parts of the process for delivery of a surveying service in which AI will be involved; if available, the extent of professional indemnity cover for use of AI systems by the firm; the internal processes to contest the use of an AI system; the processes to seek redress if a client feels they have been negatively affected by the use of an AI system, and how a client can opt out of the use of AI systems in the delivery of a surveying service, if at all.

rules.requirement_text: Firms must be able to provide, on request, written information regarding: (a) the type of AI system used, (b) basic ways of working and limitations, (c) due diligence processes carried out, (d) how risks are identified and managed, and (e) decisions made about output reliability.
rules.trigger: Client or stakeholder request for information about AI use.
rules.evidence_implied: Prepared explainability documentation covering all five items; ability to produce on request.
rules.source_text_verbatim: RICS-regulated firms must be able to provide, on request, written information regarding: the type of AI system used; the basic ways of working and limitations of the AI system used; the due diligence processes carried out before using the AI system; the way in which relevant risks associated with the use of the AI system are identified and managed, and the decisions made about the reliability of the output from the AI system.

rules.requirement_text: When developing AI systems, members and firms must apply the provisions of this standard, as required, to the development process to minimise the risk of harm.
rules.trigger: Development of an AI system by a member or firm.
rules.evidence_implied: Documentation showing how applicable provisions of the standard were applied during development.
rules.source_text_verbatim: When developing AI systems, members and RICS-regulated firms must apply the provisions of this standard, as required, to the development process to minimise the risk of harm.

rules.requirement_text: After developing and before general deployment of an AI system, members and firms must record in writing: (a) the identifiable application of the AI system, (b) the potential risks and benefits in relation to a specific task or process, and (c) other possible approaches to the same task or process.
rules.trigger: Post-development, pre-deployment of an AI system.
rules.evidence_implied: Written pre-deployment record covering application, risk/benefit analysis, and alternative approaches.
rules.source_text_verbatim: After developing, and before general deployment of an AI system, members and RICS-regulated firms must record in writing: the identifiable application of the AI system; the potential risks and benefits of the system in relation to a specific task or process, and other possible approaches to the same specific task or process.

rules.requirement_text: Members and firms developing AI systems must carry out and record in writing a sustainability impact assessment of the proposed AI system.
rules.trigger: Development of an AI system.
rules.evidence_implied: Written sustainability impact assessment document.
rules.source_text_verbatim: carry out and record in writing a sustainability impact assessment of the proposed AI system

rules.requirement_text: Members and firms developing AI systems must select a diverse range of stakeholders to be involved in the development.
rules.trigger: Establishing the project team for AI system development.
rules.evidence_implied: Stakeholder selection records; diversity documentation of project team.
rules.source_text_verbatim: select a diverse range of stakeholders to be involved in the development

rules.requirement_text: Members and firms developing AI systems must make a record of all stakeholders directly involved in the development.
rules.trigger: AI system development with stakeholder involvement.
rules.evidence_implied: Written stakeholder register for the AI development project.
rules.source_text_verbatim: make a record of all stakeholders directly involved in the development

rules.requirement_text: Members and firms developing AI systems must document the compliance of the development with all applicable data and confidentiality laws.
rules.trigger: AI system development process.
rules.evidence_implied: Legal compliance documentation; data protection impact assessment; privacy compliance records.
rules.source_text_verbatim: document the compliance of the development with all applicable data and confidentiality laws

rules.requirement_text: Members and firms must obtain written permissions from individuals where their personal data is to be used during development, in advance of the use of that data.
rules.trigger: Use of personal data in AI system development.
rules.evidence_implied: Written consent/permission records from data subjects; timestamps showing consent before data use.
rules.source_text_verbatim: obtain written permissions from individuals where their personal data is to be used during development, in advance of the use of that data for development

rules.requirement_text: Members and firms developing AI systems must have policies and processes in place to assess the quality and reliability of the data used to develop the AI system.
rules.trigger: Use of data for AI system development.
rules.evidence_implied: Data quality assessment policy; data reliability evaluation processes; quality metrics and records.
rules.source_text_verbatim: have policies and processes in place to assess the quality and reliability of the data used to develop the AI system
